analysis:
Both units are base-side text of docs/architecture/inference.md. The PR patch is documentation-only: it bumps the 'Last updated' date, adds a paragraph about the cluster service health file (DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_MEMBER_HEALTH_FILE, service-health.json versus part-health.json), and rewrites the 'Cluster runtime facts' intro so signed releases compute and register cluster_runtime approval digests. The excerpt of the patch is truncated, so I could not see all of its changes. No executable code, keys, authorization logic, or trust-boundary behavior changes in the supplied evidence, and I cite no changed lines.

One claim deserves a later look: a release computing approval digests from its own final app and registering them (cluster_runtime). This touches the approval and attestation material that coordinator-formed cluster sessions are admitted against. It resembles A-011/A-017 and TB-002/TB-011 (release registration, qualification). The implementation (release lane, backend registration, DistributedInstalledFiles, ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts) is outside the supplied evidence. I recorded this as an unverified contract and not as a finding. The same applies to the health-file environment key separation. Any code change that implements it should verify the supervisor's PID-based liveness check and that part and service heartbeat files cannot be confused or spoofed by a same-UID process.

The base excerpts cover Qwen TP media, native context, MTP and stop ordering. Those are pre-existing and unchanged by this PR, except for the Cluster runtime facts range at base lines 5221-5224, which is reworded. The rewrite introduces no new claim about a security control being weakened. No regression is identified from documentation alone. The PR's code-side changes, if any exist in other batches, still need review.
